title: Technology Sector Update for 01/09/2018: ASX,UMC,IMOS,AAPL
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -0.15%
AAPL +0.06%
IBM +0.45%
CSCO -0.28%
GOOG +0.09%
Technology stocks were still slightly underwater today, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 declining just under 0.1% today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was sinking over 0.7%.
In industry news:
+ Apple ( AAPL ) was narrowly higher Tuesday, climbing less than 0.3% to an intra-day high of $174.85 a share after the tech giant said "effectively everything" users can do on its devices can be blocked by parents. Responding to shareholder concerns over threats to children from electronic devices, Apple said it has "always looked out for kids" by creating products that "inspire, entertain and educate," an unnamed company spokeswoman told Reuters, adding it is also planning new features and enhancements in the future to improve parental control.
Among technology stocks moving on news today:
+ LRAD ( LRAD ) surged on Tuesday, touching a session high of $2.43 a share, after the maker of acoustic hailing devices and long-range audio devices today said it has received over $1 mln in new orders from customers in southeast Asia for its LRAD 100X and LRAD 500X systems along with related accessories for defense and public safety. The orders also include LRAD 1000RX remote systems for off-shore security and public safety and are scheduled to ship during the company's current fiscal year ending Sept. 30.
In other sector news:
+ Advanced Semiconductor Engineering ( ASX ) edged higher Tuesday after the chipmaker reported a 14.5% increase in Q4 revenue over year-ago levels to TWD83.99 bln - or about $2.79 bln - topping the Capital IQ consensus by around TWD2.59 bln.
- United Microelectronics ( UMC ) fell today after reporting a 15% sales drop compared with year-ago levels to NTD10.67 bln during December. For all of FY17, sales grew 1%.
- ChipMOS ( IMOS ) declined after saying revenue fell 11.1% year-over-year in December to NT$1.41 bln - or about $47.6 mln. Q4 revenue was down 5.5% to NT$4.41 bln.
